protocol: D-000 new cycle, turn 1 of 3; refute not confirm; RULE-GOVERNED coordinator recording of an independently ACCEPTed candidate, in the adopted D-035 / D-038 / D-042 form
summary: Subject and prompt held at their dispatched digests, both read-only. This entry does one thing and refuses everything adjacent to it. The central attack — treating an ACCEPT verdict as owner recording — fails in the entry's own operative text and is additionally rejected by name in the alternatives section. I was able to verify one digest here absolutely rather than by corroboration: the entry pins my v2 verdict at d5c1eccd…, which is the file I authored, and its recital 'ACCEPT 0/0' is exactly what that verdict returned. All five cited digests match live bytes, DR-010's HARD-BLOCKED standing is confirmed in file 08, and the entry's characterisation of the candidate — seven items EXCLUDED or NOT REPLACED, P-1/P-2/G3-SUBSTRATE preserved, CD-RT-5 untouched — is accurate against the candidate's own fields.
whatIVerified: Subject digest at start and end: c1de9b3c6e025f56f27a137d1e2cc702a4b7bced9b96e2449549866e0b11198f, three measurements at start and again at end, equal to the dispatched frozen digest, -r--r--r-- at both ends. Prompt held at ce9121c53d8ff2b65b2b768aa54d9dc4077e7aeb82e7ea2f1684377e7148dafb, also read-only.

The attack 'treats ACCEPT as owner recording' fails twice over. Clause 2 states 'This is not owner recording. An ACCEPT verdict is not owner recording. DR-010 stays HARD-BLOCKED. Condition 1 does not discharge until the product owner records.' The header independently states 'Does not owner-record.' And the alternatives section names the error and rejects it: 'Treat ACCEPT as owner recording. Rejected.' This is also consistent with the pinned candidate, which itself says 'This file existing, or an ACCEPT verdict, is not owner recording.'

The attack 'silent SATISFIED or condition-1 discharge' fails. The header refuses SATISFIED, clause 2 makes condition-1 discharge conditional on a future act by the product owner, clause 3 states 'Does not mark SATISFIED. Does not edit file 08. Conditions 2–5 remain. Condition 5 remains the only implementation authorization', and the readiness effect is 'Zero.' I confirmed the premise rather than accepting it: file 08's DR-010 status cell reads HARD-BLOCKED, so 'DR-010 stays HARD-BLOCKED' is a true statement about current standing.

The attack 'closes DR-117 / R16' fails. Clause 2 holds 'DR-117 and DR-011-R16 stay independently required', and the alternatives section rejects the bundling explicitly: 'Also close DR-117 / R16 here. Rejected: bundling; those remain independently required.'

I verified the entry's characterisation of the candidate against the candidate's own fields rather than taking the summary on trust. Its seven previewDisposition values are EXCLUDED, EXCLUDED, EXCLUDED, EXCLUDED, 'EXCLUDED as contribution roles', EXCLUDED and NOT REPLACED — six exclusions and one not-replaced, which is exactly what clause 1's 'EXCLUDED or NOT REPLACED' asserts. The candidate's preservedV1Decisions carries P-1, P-2 and G3-SUBSTRATE, and both its enforcementHonesty and whatThisDoesNotDo leave CD-RT-5 untouched.

All five cited digests match live bytes: COORD d0284aab…, file 08 6547e6ac…, the candidate product-boundary-preview.v2.json at ff7a0913…, my own verdict at d5c1eccd…, and the Codex verdict at 8b64732c…. The candidate digest is the same value I measured at both ends of my v2 review, so the artifact being recorded is byte-identical to the artifact I reviewed.

The recital of my own verdict is exact, and this is the one reviewer-verdict claim in this corpus I can test absolutely rather than corroborate. The entry cites 'ACCEPT 0/0'; the file at that digest is the one I wrote, and it records verdict ACCEPT with 0 blockers and 0 advisories.

The form citation 'Same form as D-035 / D-038 / D-042' is accurate. All three are present in COORD, ADOPTED, and are the same coordinator-recording class: D-035 records doctor-contract.v4 as DR-114's accepted design contract, D-038 records host-effect-authorization.v8 as the accepted host-effect design contract, and D-042 records permission-truth-tables.v2 as DR-105's accepted design-contract candidate. The 'Total' reversibility matches D-038's and D-042's.

Examined and cleared: the entry records the candidate as 'DR-010's accepted Route C design-candidate' although the candidate's own registerRows lists DR-010, DR-117 and DR-011-R16. This is a deliberate, disclosed narrowing rather than a silent one — clause 2 holds the other two rows independently required and the alternatives section rejects closing them — and narrowing is the conservative direction for a recording that binds nothing.

Examined and cleared: the entry does not mention that v2 supersedes v1 or that v1's review produced two repaired advisories. I checked the convention rather than assuming one. D-038 and D-042 are themselves recordings of a .v8 and a .v2 and neither mentions a prior version, so recording only the accepted version is the established form. The lineage is not lost either way: the pinned candidate carries predecessor and predecessorSha256 pointing at v1 at 060220c0…, so the digest pin incorporates it.

No advisory classification clause is required here and none is missing. Both verdicts on the candidate are clean ACCEPT at 0/0, so there is no advisory to classify as operative or non-operative — unlike the D-060 recording, which needed that clause because one reviewer returned ACCEPT-WITH-ADVISORIES.

The attacks 'condition 5 / docs/v2/implementation' and 'file 08 edited' fail: the header refuses to authorize docs/v2/implementation/, clause 3 preserves condition 5 as the only implementation authorization and refuses the file 08 edit, file 08 measures unchanged at its cited digest, and git reports zero modified tracked files. I wrote one file and edited and committed nothing.
whatIDidNotCheck: The Codex review of this subject. Not read; the file is confirmed absent at review time.

The Codex review of product-boundary-preview.v2. Its digest verifies at 8b64732c… but I did not open it, so the recital 'ACCEPT 0/0' on that side rests on this entry's statement. My own recital I verified absolutely.
Whether the product owner, as a human, would record the disposition. That act is what clause 2 defers, and it is outside this entry.

The merits of product-boundary-preview.v2 beyond my separate ACCEPT review of it, whose stated limits I carry forward — including that I did not audit the qualification gates DR-G07, DR-G08, DR-G09, DR-G21, DR-128 or DR-110 for what they require, only that they exist and that the DR-G08/DR-110 scope split the candidate asserts is accurate.
DR-117's and DR-011-R16's specific content. This entry leaves both independently required, which is the conservative disposition, but I did not audit either.

environment.measurementTool: shasum -a 256 of subject and prompt three times at start and again at end with ls -l for permissions at both ends; digest verification of all five cited inputs against live bytes; json parse of my own v2 verdict to test the 'ACCEPT 0/0' recital against its actual verdict, blockers and advisories fields; json parse of the candidate for its seven previewDisposition values, preservedV1Decisions, registerRows, predecessor and predecessorSha256; regex extraction of D-035, D-038 and D-042 from COORD to test the form citation, their adoption status, their reversibility class and whether any mentions a prior artifact version; field extraction of file 08's DR-010 status cell; git status across the tree

consentNote: I CONSENT with zero MUST-FIX and zero SHOULD-FIX. The distinction this entry exists to hold — that an independent ACCEPT records a candidate but does not record it as an owner — is stated in the operative clause, restated in the header, rejected by name in the alternatives, and consistent with the candidate's own text. DR-010 stays HARD-BLOCKED, which I confirmed against file 08 rather than accepting. I note with some satisfaction that this entry pins reviewer-verdict digests, which is what I asked for in my D-051-053 turn-3 note; it let me verify one recital absolutely instead of corroborating it, because the file it names at d5c1eccd… is the one I wrote.
